passages.text: Now about the collection for the saints, you are to do as I directed the churches of Galatia: On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside a portion of his income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will be needed.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the church in Corinth.
He spoke about the collection for the saints.
Paul had already given instructions to the churches in Galatia.
He told the Corinthians to do the same.
On the first day of every week, each person should set aside money.
Each person should save a portion of his income.
Each person should do this regularly.
This way, when Paul comes, no collections will be needed.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῆς λογείας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους ὥσπερ διέταξα ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιήσατε κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου ἕκαστος ὑμῶν παρ’ ἑαυτῷ τιθέτω θησαυρίζων ὅ¦τι ἐὰν εὐοδῶται ἵνα μὴ ὅταν ἔλθω τότε λογεῖαι γίνωνται

passages.text: Then, on my arrival, I will send letters with those you recommend to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul will come to visit them.
Paul tells them to choose people they trust.
They should recommend these people by letter.
Paul will send these recommended people to Jerusalem.
They will carry the gift from the church in Corinth to Jerusalem.
passages.original: ὅταν δὲ παραγένωμαι οὓς ἐὰν δοκιμάσητε δι’ ἐπιστολῶν τούτους πέμψω ἀπενεγκεῖν τὴν χάριν ὑμῶν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: And if it is advisable for me to go also, they can travel with me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul discusses the collection for the saints in Jerusalem.
Paul says, "If it is best for me to go also, I will go."
The people you choose can travel with me.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ ἄξιον ᾖ τοῦ κἀμὲ πορεύεσθαι σὺν ἐμοὶ πορεύσονται

passages.text: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthians.
Paul plans to visit the Corinthians.
Paul will travel through Macedonia first.
Paul will come to the Corinthians after he goes through Macedonia.
Paul is going through Macedonia.
passages.original: Ἐλεύσομαι δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅταν Μακεδονίαν διέλθω Μακεδονίαν γὰρ διέρχομαι

passages.text: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul may stay with the believers in Corinth for a while.
Paul may even spend the winter with them.
Paul wants the believers to help him on his journey.
Paul will need their help wherever he goes next.
passages.original: πρὸς ὑμᾶς δὲ τυχὸν παραμενῶ ἢ καὶ παραχειμάσω ἵνα ὑμεῖς με προπέμψητε οὗ ἐὰν πορεύωμαι

passages.text: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthians.
Paul does not want to visit them only for a short time.
Paul hopes to stay with them for a while.
Paul will stay if the Lord allows it.
passages.original: οὐ θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἄρτι ἐν παρόδῳ ἰδεῖν ἐλπίζω γὰρ χρόνον τινὰ ἐπιμεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος ἐπιτρέψῃ

passages.text: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost, because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul will stay in Ephesus.
He will stay until Pentecost.
God has opened a great door for Paul.
This door is for effective work.
Many people oppose Paul.
passages.original: ἐπιμενῶ δὲ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἕως τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς θύρα γάρ μοι ἀνέῳγεν μεγάλη καὶ ἐνεργής καὶ ἀντικείμενοι πολλοί

passages.text: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.
passages.sermon:
Timothy is a fellow worker for the Lord.
If Timothy comes to you, watch over him.
Make sure Timothy has nothing to fear while he is with you.
Timothy does the work of the Lord.
I also do the work of the Lord.
Treat Timothy as you would treat me.
passages.original: Ἐὰν δὲ ἔλθῃ Τιμόθεος βλέπετε ἵνα ἀφόβως γένηται πρὸς ὑμᾶς τὸ γὰρ ἔργον Κυρίου ἐργάζεται ὡς κἀγώ

passages.text: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.
passages.sermon:
Timothy is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.
No one should treat Timothy with contempt.
Send Timothy on his way in peace.
Then he can return to me.
I am expecting him to come with the brothers.
passages.original: μή τις οὖν αὐτὸν ἐξουθενήσῃ προπέμψατε δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρός με ἐκδέχομαι γὰρ αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν

passages.text: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.
passages.sermon:
Apollos is our brother.
I strongly urged Apollos to visit you.
I asked him to go with the other brothers.
Apollos did not want to go now.
He will go when he has the opportunity.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ πολλὰ παρεκάλεσα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν καὶ πάντως οὐκ ἦν θέλημα ἵνα νῦν ἔλθῃ ἐλεύσεται δὲ ὅταν εὐκαιρήσῃ

passages.text: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.
passages.sermon:
Be alert.
Stand firm in the faith.
Show courage.
Be strong.
passages.original: Γρηγορεῖτε στήκετε ἐν τῇ πίστει ἀνδρίζεσθε κραταιοῦσθε

passages.text: Do everything in love.
passages.sermon: You must do everything.\r\nYou must act in love.\r\nLet all your actions come from love.
passages.original: πάντα ὑμῶν ἐν ἀγάπῃ γινέσθω

passages.text: You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Now I urge you, brothers, to submit to such as these, and to every fellow worker and laborer.
passages.sermon:
Stephanas and his household were the first people in Achaia to believe in Christ.
They devoted themselves to serving the saints.
You know this.
Brothers, I urge you to submit to people like them.
Submit also to every fellow worker.
Submit to every person who works hard.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί οἴδατε τὴν οἰκίαν Στεφανᾶ ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀχαΐας καὶ εἰς διακονίαν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἔταξαν ἑαυτούς ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ὑποτάσσησθε τοῖς τοιούτοις καὶ παντὶ τῷ συνεργοῦντι καὶ κοπιῶντι

passages.text: I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this message to the church in Corinth.
Paul is the author.
Paul feels glad.
Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived.
These three men came to Paul.
The church in Corinth could not give Paul everything he needed.
Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus supplied what the church lacked.
They brought what was missing from the church.
Paul is thankful for their arrival and their help.
passages.original: Χαίρω δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ παρουσίᾳ Στεφανᾶ καὶ Φορτουνάτου καὶ Ἀχαϊκοῦ ὅτι τὸ ὑμέτερον ὑστέρημα οὗτοι ἀνεπλήρωσαν

passages.text: For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men.
passages.sermon:
Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus refreshed my spirit.
They also refreshed your spirit.
Recognize men like these.
Show your appreciation to them.
passages.original: ἀνέπαυσαν γὰρ τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν ἐπιγινώσκετε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους

passages.text: The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.
passages.sermon:
The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings.
Aquila greets you warmly in the Lord.
Prisca greets you warmly in the Lord.
The church that meets at their house also greets you.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῆς Ἀσίας Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἐν Κυρίῳ πολλὰ Ἀκύλας καὶ Πρίσκα σὺν τῇ κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίᾳ

passages.text: All the brothers here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
passages.sermon: All the brothers here send you greetings.\r\nGreet one another with a holy kiss.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες Ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ

passages.text: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul.
passages.sermon: Paul writes this greeting himself.\r\nPaul uses his own hand to write this greeting.
passages.original: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου

passages.text: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse. Come, O Lord!
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul speaks to the church.
Paul says, "If anyone does not love the Lord, let that person be under a curse."
Paul says, "Come, O Lord!"
passages.original: Εἴ τις οὐ φιλεῖ τὸν Κύριον ἤτω ἀνάθεμα Μαράνα θά

passages.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
passages.sermon:
The Lord Jesus gives grace.
Grace is a gift from the Lord Jesus.
I pray that this grace stays with you.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
passages.original: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ μεθ’ ὑμῶν

passages.text: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer of this letter.
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul says, "My love is with all of you."
Paul says this love is in Christ Jesus.
Paul ends with, "Amen."
passages.original: Ἡ ἀγάπη μου μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ Ἀμήν
